item.title: Lightspeed shoes: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Doctor Ramses, per the Site's Criticism Policy found here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/criticism-policy

Forum critique should be relatively in-depth.

Try to make sure you give enough criticism that an author can tell the quality of their entire concept/draft. Did you like it because it reminds you of Dado or GAW? How does this concept remind you of Dado and GAW? What changes would you suggest? What could make this concept better? What should be kept? What should be discarded? Do you personally see this as something successful on the site? Please try to endeavour in writing a more detailed analysis when dropping critique in the future, as it would be of a better benefit to the author.

If you need more assistance with how to properly write a review, please consider referring to this thread for guidance: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-9804362/so-you-want-to-be-a-concept-reviewer

Also,

You'll want to edit this to fit the format though, don't wanna piss off the mods.

I can’t speak for the entirety of staff, but I’m confident that something like forgetting the template won’t cause feelings of anger among staff. It’s a pretty common mistake. Thank you for addressing the author about the template though! :)

sandtshark, since this thread has been disrupted, please consider referring to this thread if you are in need of a reviewer:
http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Nechronometer: Forum Criticism Team - Junior Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
Pau_Gaba, per the Site's Criticism Policy found here: http://www.scp-wiki.net/criticism-policy

Criticism should be helpful in some way.

Try to give the author an idea of where to take their concept/draft, or what might make their current article better. What about the concept looks curious? What did you find interesting about it? What would you suggest would help this concept to its full potential? Should the concept stay simple and weird, or should that change? If so, in which ways should it change? Which parts specifically should the author expand on more? Please try to offer a more detailed response in the future when dropping critique. It would better help the author if the critique was more specific and direct, so the author knows exactly what to modify and/or keep within their idea.

If you need more assistance with how to properly write a review, please consider referring to this thread for guidance: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-9804362/so-you-want-to-be-a-concept-reviewer

item.title: Nechronometer: Re: Nechronometer
item.content:encoded:
This could be interesting, but you didn't really give us a narrative only a plot point. I'm going to need some more info on the entire story your trying to tell to judge correctly.

But based on what you have here, there going to be some explanation on why the Foundation is using an anomaly for their team and maybe on what that means for her. Or this could a canon where the Foundation will use anomalous means to deal with threats accordingly.

item.title: Woodbones: Re: Woodbones
item.content:encoded:
Naim will tell his story of first resenting SCP-XXXX but eventually becoming fond and reliant on it. It will then follow how Naim won countless Gold medals and weightlifting titles in the Olympics.

&

Much of the article will be Naim explaining conversations with SCP-XXXX while it was inside of him. He will explain its goals and thoughts and why it does what it does in interviews with SCP researchers while it is still inside of him.

This will be a huge exposition dump. How do you intend to communicate these things without just "telling" the reader what they need to know?

item.title: A Complete Group: A Complete Group
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A total of 49 tombs(and one vacant tomb) located underground. The bodies belonged to a group of reality benders who could 'bless' (call it what you will) chosen areas and prevent anyone within those areas from ever getting injured or killed. As of now,their corpses now 'curse' people within 20 meters of them. It was something not even they knew the reason for.

Central Narrative: The story will begin with the only known survivor of the group being discovered and interviewed in the former headquarters of the group. The survivor explains that over 23 years,they have researched and logged all areas affected by their 'blessings' in order to see where the best places to bless would be.

He further explains that the reason they have all passed away was due to the leader.(Who he refers to as "The Willow") Her death caused a chain reaction upon all the members of the group to perish,leaving only the unnamed survivor to bury them.

Hook: If you enjoy stories about the history of abandoned places,this could definitely intrigue you if I do it right. In the end,its a simple story about the past of a group of people.

Additional Notes:
•The article will include the logs and research created by their group
•In the article,the survivor will state that his curse was the inability to leave the Headquarters and the tombs.He states that "the others were not so lucky."

•If there is anything that seems off,please tell me.

item.title: Hello. This is the third refinement of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: Hello. This is the third refinement of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you: Hello. This is the third refinement of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A pale, smooth-skinned humanoid, approximately 2 feet tall. It has keen sight despite having no eyes. Despite having no limbs, it tries to move using it's torso. It shows aggression at the morning, and immobility at night. Every time a subject touches it, they will start to decay.

Central Narrative: none

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A humanoid creature that can decay any material.

item.title: Hi! This is the revised version of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you!: Re: Hi! This is the revised version of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you!
item.content:encoded: This could use some elaborating. It can only move its head and torso, but it's swift? Does it float around? The idea of an SCP that decays things is interesting, but it also making duplicates might be too much. Then again, it could make sense if it was absorbing the nutrients to clone itself. I don't see the need for it to be a statue of a human too, any kind of strange living creature could work. Either way, the idea could use some refinement, but it has good potential.

item.title: The innate nature of things.: Re: The innate nature of things.
item.content:encoded: I'm still a newcomer here, but I like it. The idea of a physical space that represents fundamental laws in our universe is pretty fascinating. I also like the narrative potential with the previous universe and some of the machinery being broken. Not sure about the cosmic horror aspect, since its difficult to pull off effectively, but this seems like an idea that's definitely worth writing. Also, to me, this seems like something that could potentially be so integral to the SCP universe that it may be a decent candidate for 001. Again, still new, so take my opinion for whatever it's worth.

item.title: Hi! This is the revised version of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you!: Hi! This is the revised version of my idea, Please tell me your opinion. Thank you!
item.content:encoded: A sculpture of a human, approximately 2 feet tall. It has keen sight despite having no eyes. It is swift despite having no limbs. It shows aggression at the morning, and immobility at night. It can move it's head, and torso. Every time a subject touches the sculpture, they will start to decay. It can make duplicates of itself, using it's body. It can make duplicates of itself by growing an instance at it's torso. The instance, even though it isn't fully grown, can also decay subjects. Every instance will have the decaying effect to subjects.
